answer: Securing an AI agent economy against Sybil attacks requires tying network influence to verifiable computational work, creating a steep economic canyon that deters mass identity forgery. When agents face a sudden gale of malicious bot generation, decentralized validation protocols impose cryptographic proof-of-stake or hardware-bound resource costs. This forces the marginal cost of creating fake nodes to spike sharply, driving attacker profitability toward its structural nadir and preserving protocol integrity.
